checks: Greedy vectors have nondecreasing lengths because the allowable complements shrink. The independent-vector argument gives the successive minima and the highest nonzero flag coordinate proves separation at least one after coordinate rescaling.

An open ball of radius 1/2 injects into the torus. Its volume gives product of the greedy lengths at most 2^r times the lattice covolume divided by the unit-ball volume. The determinant functional is integer on the full lattice regardless of the index of the generated sublattice.

Hadamard bounds the determinant functional by the product of the first r−1 lengths divided by the covolume. Coefficient rounding in the generated sublattice bounds the covering radius by r times the last length divided by two, giving C_r and its elementary cube bound, including the empty product at r=1.

A dual functional takes integer-spaced levels on the coset, regardless of primality. The support projection width bounds their count by 1+2R times the dual norm, with the 1 outside the product. The actual weighted mass of each level is at most xi of the total, yielding the stated xi/(1−xi) factor.
The section Jacobian |det C| and optional covolume factor |det A| are constant across fine bases. Pullback is a bijection of affine fine hyperplanes. Counting in dimension zero uses Jacobian one.

The three samples are the complete lattice census of [0,2h]. They are equally weighted; the endpoints alone generate the entire product body. In the unit-spacing centered frame R=1, xi=1/3, rho=1/2, and C_1=1/2. In any block frame the fine width is 2|A|h, so an inner radius b forces rho≥b/2.

overlap.comparison: For section measures with convex superlevels this accepted theorem lower-bounds one hyperplane’s mass using sampled/coarse volume and a greedy base selection. It gives neither the dual-spacing/covering-radius inequality nor the bound for arbitrary finite positive weights.

The determinant identity for vertical-preserving transforms specializes to the same common section factor. Its conclusion concerns geometry and normalized sampled depth, not the quantitative hyperplane-to-mesh implication.
